title: CI regression coverage mapper for sequence-shape drift across streaming + toolcall flows
creator: Jordan Patel
description: Add an automated mapper and CI checks that exercise API surface variants which cause 'sequence-shape drift' (changes in tokenization, chunking, or multipart framing) across streaming responses and tool/function-calling flows. The goal is to detect regressions where minor runtime or kernel changes alter chunk boundaries or field ordering such that downstream tool parsers or structured-output validators begin failing intermittently.
background: We have intermittent post-deploy fails in downstream tool integrations that only manifest when streaming chunk boundaries shift (e.g., KV cache priming tokens crossing chunk edges or tool call metadata emitted in a different chunk). Existing golden-prompt suites catch behavioral drift at a high level, but they do not cover the combinatorial space of sequence shapes (chunk sizes, partial-json boundaries, interleaving of toolcall tokens). On-call runs have shown flakiness in canaries after kernel swaps and quantization changes. We need a CI-level mapper that generates representative variants and asserts deterministic parsing of structured outputs and toolcall boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: A CI job that generates at least 3,000 sequence-shape variants per model/endpoint combination and runs in < 25m on CI runner.

For streaming endpoints, assert that structured-output JSON schemas and function call signatures are complete and re-assemblable despite chunk boundary perturbations (zero false negatives on golden seed set).
Integrate a flakiness detector that marks test seeds with >10% non-deterministic failures as 'flaky' and records a fingerprint for triage.
Test runner produces machine-readable report (NDJSON) with per-seed fingerprint, failing assertion, model revision, and environment tags; artifact uploaded to CI build.
Create a dashboard queryable by fingerprint to correlate failures with runtime rollouts / kernel versions.
Add gating: PRs to runtime that increase flaky seeds by >5% must be blocked until an owner signoff or a mitigation is merged.
tasks: Design: define sequence-shape mutation matrix (chunk sizes, offset shifts, tokenization split points, injected backpressure events)
Prototype: mutation engine that replays a canonical prompt and emits N mutated streams with preserved content semantics
Implement: CI job that runs mutations across the matrix and asserts structured-output roundtrip + function call idempotency
Report: NDJSON artifact schema spec and upload hook for CI
Observability: add dashboard panels and fingerprint index in Console trace storage
Docs: short runbook for triaging fingerprinted failures and labeling flaky seeds
Rollout: enable as optional job on canary pipeline, then promote to required gate after 2 weeks of stabilization
implementation_notes: Mutation engine will operate at the transport layer: split canonical response at token boundaries computed using the same tokenizer as model runtime, then re-chunk by varying target byte/token counts.
Prefer deterministic token split algorithm using runtime tokenizer binary to avoid false positives from tokenizer drift.
Use lightweight emulation (no full model inference) by replaying captured model outputs (golden seeds) for seed generation; this keeps CI runtime small while exercising streamer assembly logic.
For tool/function call checks, validate that the reassembled stream produces identical structured payloads (method name, args schema) and that toolcall ids remain stable.
Record environment tags: runtime-commit, kernel-version, model-checkpoint, quantization-profile, ci-image-hash.
Keep the initial seed corpus limited to high-signal prompts (20 seeds), expand after initial run to cover edgecases found in incident logs.
Make mutation matrix configurable via JSON so product or SRE can add new perturbations without code changes.
test_plan: Phase 1: run mutation engine locally against captured golden responses. Validate reassembly and schema parsing for 20 seeds.
Phase 2: CI job on canary runs nightly for 2 weeks; collect fingerprints and surface top-10 flakiest seeds.
Phase 3: require job in merge checks for runtime PRs that touch streaming, kernel scheduling, or kv cache logic.
Assertions: structured-output validator (jsonschema), functioncall signature checker, and token-level checksum equality for non-streamed canonical outputs.
Performance constraint: CI job must parallelize seeds and use cached artifacts to keep wall time under 25 minutes.
dependencies: A small infra task to add NDJSON artifact retention to CI storage (infra-ticket TBD)
